issues.t: Brake booster pump failure with ABS and brake lights
issues.sym: The brake, ABS and traction lights come on, sometimes with a Check VSC message. The pedal can feel soft or sink, braking takes longer, you may hear the brake pump buzzing often, and cruise control may switch off. Common codes are C1391, C1252, C1253 and C1256.
issues.why: The electric brake booster and its pump on the Prius c wear out and leak pressure from the accumulator, so the car loses power-assisted braking. Toyota ran a customer support program (21TE01) for 2012-2014 models, but its main coverage ended in November 2022.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Treat this as urgent: leave more stopping distance and get the brakes checked right away. Ask a Toyota dealer whether your car still qualifies for the 10-year/150,000-mile part of the support program before paying for the repair.

issues.t: ABS and brake lights from failing brake actuator
issues.sym: The ABS, brake and other warning lights come on, often with code C1391. Pumping the brake pedal may turn the red brake light off for a while, and the lights can come and go.
issues.why: The brake booster, pump or ABS actuator in the Prius v's electronically controlled brake system loses pressure as it ages, usually past 100,000 miles. Owners report dealers replacing the ABS actuator and booster parts.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Get the codes read promptly. Ask a Toyota dealer to check for any open support program on your VIN.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, sometimes a quart every 600-1,000 miles, and the low oil light may flash. It usually shows up after about 70,000-100,000 miles, with no visible leaks.
issues.why: Worn or carbon-stuck piston rings in the 1.8L engine let oil burn off in the cylinders. Some owners had a head gasket fail before or alongside the oil burning.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and keep it topped off; running low can ruin the engine. Ask a Toyota dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any warranty help applies. A fix usually means new pistons and rings or a replacement engine.

issues.t: Head gasket failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, misfire or rough running, and sometimes coolant loss, overheating or white exhaust smoke. Owners report it between about 90,000 and 150,000 miles.
issues.why: The head gasket on the 1.8L engine can leak coolant into a cylinder. Owners and mechanics often link it to a clogged EGR system that makes the engine run hotter.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs or coolant keeps dropping. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and look for coolant in the cylinders. Ask them to clean the EGR parts during the repair.

issues.t: Inverter can overheat and limit power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights come on and the car goes into a reduced-power limp mode that only lets you drive a short distance. In some cases the hybrid system shuts off while driving.
issues.why: A part inside the hybrid inverter can overheat. Toyota updated the motor/generator and hybrid control software to prevent it.
issues.next: Check your VIN on Toyota's recall site. The software update is free at a Toyota dealer.

issues.t: Hybrid system can shut down and stall (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights come on and the car loses drive power while moving, possibly coasting to a stop. Steering and brakes still work.
issues.why: Too much voltage in a power module inside the hybrid inverter can make the hybrid system shut down. Toyota recalled 2012-2014 models (18V-684) and then 2014-2017 models (20V-369).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the hybrid software for free and repairs or replaces the inverter if it has already failed.

issues.t: Hybrid battery cooling fan clogged with dust
issues.sym: A hybrid battery cooling warning, a louder battery fan, lower fuel economy, or a check engine light, often on cars that carry pets or drive in dusty areas.
issues.why: The fan that cools the hybrid battery pulls air from the cabin through a small filter near the rear seat. Dust and pet hair clog the filter and fan, so the battery runs hot and wears faster.
issues.next: Have the hybrid battery fan filter and fan cleaned, and check the filter every year or two. This is simple maintenance that helps the hybrid battery last longer.

issues.t: Hybrid battery wearing out
issues.sym: Check engine and hybrid system warning lights, code P0A80 (replace hybrid battery pack), worse fuel economy, and the engine running more often than it used to.
issues.why: The nickel-metal hydride hybrid battery slowly loses capacity with age, heat and mileage. Once some cells weaken, the car flags the pack for replacement.
issues.next: Have a hybrid shop test the battery. Check whether Toyota's hybrid battery warranty still covers your car. New, remanufactured and used packs are all options.

issues.t: Car won't go into READY mode
issues.sym: You press the power button but the READY light doesn't come on, the dash shows a shift-to-park message even though you're in park, and the car won't drive. Trying again later often works.
issues.why: Owners report this as an intermittent fault, sometimes after the car has sat in the hot sun; a weak 12-volt battery or brake/shift position signals are common causes of no-READY conditions on Toyota hybrids.
issues.next: Press the brake firmly, make sure it's in park, and try again. Have the 12-volt battery tested, and if it keeps happening, ask a dealer to read stored codes.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P2610
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P2610 (engine off timer performance), with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A logic problem in the engine control computer's internal timer sets a false code. Toyota released a bulletin with a computer update.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer confirm the code and apply the update from the bulletin. It won't hurt the car short-term, but a lit check engine light can hide new problems.

issues.t: Musty or chemical smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A mildew, musty or sharp chemical smell when the A/C or fan runs, sometimes from new.
issues.why: Moisture left on the A/C evaporator lets mold and bacteria grow, and a clogged A/C drain tube can trap water. Toyota has bulletins for HVAC odors and blocked drain tubes.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter, have the A/C drain tube checked, and ask about an evaporator cleaning. Running the fan without A/C for a few minutes before parking helps dry it out.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from compressor or condenser failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or hot air even when set to cold.
issues.why: The Prius c uses an electric A/C compressor that can fail, and the condenser up front can leak. One owner had the compressor fail just past 31,000 miles, right after the basic warranty ended.
issues.next: Have a shop check the refrigerant level and look for leaks first. Hybrid A/C compressors need a special oil, so use a shop that services hybrids.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out often
issues.sym: Low-beam headlight bulbs, and sometimes tail lights, burn out every few weeks or months.
issues.why: Owners haven't found a clear cause; bulbs failing this often point to a bulb quality, voltage or connector problem.
issues.next: Replace both low beams with quality bulbs and avoid touching the glass. If they keep failing, have a shop check the voltage and the headlight connectors for heat damage.

issues.t: Dim headlights at night
issues.sym: The headlights don't light up the road well, making night driving hard.
issues.why: Owners say the stock halogen headlights on the Prius c give a weak, short beam.
issues.next: Have the headlight aim checked, clean or restore cloudy lenses, and consider higher-output legal replacement bulbs.

issues.t: Brakes grab or release oddly in wet weather
issues.sym: In rain, the brakes feel very sensitive or grabby, or the rear brakes seem to let go at low speed.
issues.why: The car blends regenerative braking with the friction brakes and ABS. On wet roads the system can switch between them abruptly, which some owners feel as grabbing or a brief release.
issues.next: Brake smoothly and leave extra distance in the rain. If it feels like the brakes let go or the warning lights come on, have the brake system checked right away.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor out of calibration (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may show the wrong setting for who is in the seat.
issues.why: The front passenger seat's occupant sensing system was out of calibration, so the airbag might not deploy, or might deploy when it shouldn't.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer recalibrates the system for free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light may come on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The occupant classification system that turns the passenger airbag on or off may be miscalibrated, so the airbag could stay off in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer recalibrates the system for free.

issues.t: Windshield cracks easily
issues.sym: A crack spreads across the windshield from a tiny chip, or appears with no clear impact, sometimes on a fairly new car.
issues.why: Owners report the Prius v windshield cracks more easily than expected; the large, steeply raked glass can spread cracks from small stone chips.
issues.next: Repair chips quickly before they spread, and check whether your insurance covers glass. Use OEM or equal-quality glass so the rain sensor and mounts fit right.

issues.t: Touchscreen unresponsive or radio acting up
issues.sym: The center touchscreen ignores taps or acts on its own, and the radio or audio stops working properly.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the Entune audio head unit; software glitches or a failing unit are the usual causes.
issues.next: Try a reset by turning the car fully off for a few minutes. Ask a dealer about software updates; a failing head unit may need repair or replacement.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning light may not come on when a tire is low.
issues.why: The tire pressure monitoring system on a small number of cars was calibrated wrong, so it may miss underinflated tires.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and check tire pressures monthly yourself. The dealer fixes the system for free.

issues.t: Spare tire may be under-inflated from the factory (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom until you need the spare, which may be low on air.
issues.why: On a small batch of cars, the spare tire wasn't filled to the pressure on the tire label.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls, or simply check the spare's pressure yourself. The dealer inspects and inflates it for free.

issues.t: DC-DC converter can fail and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights come on, the 12-volt battery runs down, and the car can lose drive power.
issues.why: The DC-DC converter, which charges the 12-volt battery from the hybrid battery, may fail. Without it, the 12-volt battery drains and the car can shut down.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the DC-DC converter for free if needed.

issues.t: Airbag warning label missing (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the airbag warning label on the sun visor or dash may be missing.
issues.why: A small number of cars were built without the required airbag warning label.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs the label for free.
